name: The Andrus household — a name from the post office's letter lists
head: andrus_thomas

arrival.note: A BOUND FROM THE RETURN, NOT AN ARRIVAL. The office's list of letters uncalled-for is a RETURN — its statement of what was still unclaimed on ONE day — and the paper reprinted one return over as many consecutive issues as it took, so the bound is dated by the return of March 1835 and not by the issue it was read in (T-0425). The earliest issue this project reads the name in is 1835-05-20, 50 days later; that gap is an accident of which impression an extraction pass reached, and it is not evidence. Somebody was writing to this name at Chicago by 1835-03-31 and at no stated time before it; nothing says when they came. The date lines the printings set, and how they were weighed, stand beside this rule in tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py.

lives_at.note: Not attested: a letter list gives a name and no address.

works_at.note: Not attested. No trade is recorded, so there is no premises to seek.

present_on_scene_date.note: THE CORPUS STOPS BEFORE THE SCENE DATE. Nothing after 1835-05-20 follows this person to 1 July 1835 or says they left. `uncertain` rather than dropped — the distinction index.json draws for Jeremiah Porter, and a finding, not a gap.

persons.name: Thomas Andrus

occupation.note: T-0485: independently corroborated resident research. DuPage history gives a detailed chronology for Thomas Andrus: arrival in Chicago Dec. 1, 1833, carpenter/pile-driving work in 1834, return east in autumn 1834, and arrival back at Chicago in June 1835 before settling in DuPage in July. This independently identifies the exact person behind the regional postal seed.

persons.note: INDEPENDENTLY CORROBORATED RESIDENT. Originally documented in Chicago post-office evidence; independent resident research now corroborates the identity. KNOWN ONLY FROM THE POST OFFICE, IN ONE RETURN. The papers print 'Andrus, Tomas' in a single return of letters uncalled-for at the Chicago post office — the Democrat of 20 May 1835, column 13 — dated 1835-05-20. WHAT THAT IS WORTH: a correspondent believed a person of this name reachable at Chicago on that date, and nothing further — not that they lived here, kept a trade here, or were here on 1 July 1835. It is the weakest evidence this project accepts for a resident, and a source placing them elsewhere retires the record. THE ARGUMENT EVERY RECORD OF THIS KIND SHARES is written once instead of once per file: the ruling of 2026-08-30 and what it cost the town (docs/LIBERTIES.md L214), the refusals and the transcription standard behind the reading (tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py). No figure is drawn (L1).

refusals.reason: This card rests on 1 thing(s) the consolidation did not read — rr_dupage_andrus_1882. G3 fired on the seven domains the ladder reads and says nothing about the evidence outside them, so the grade stands. The same reasoning the ladder's own G5 gives for abstaining (T-0515).

profile_facts.note: The DuPage history gives a day, and the household's own arrival block is explicit that its 1835-03-31 is a BOUND FROM THE RETURN and not an arrival. The two are different claims about different things and both stand; the bound is not touched.

profile_facts.value: Returned east in the autumn of 1834
profile_facts.note: A dated leaving, carried as a life event. It does not move present_on_scene_date, which stays 'uncertain' on its own reasoning.

profile_facts.as_read: arrival back at Chicago in June 1835
profile_facts.note: The month before the scene date, from the same chronology. Recorded as the source states it and not converted into presence on 1 July.

profile_facts.as_read: before settling in DuPage in July
profile_facts.note: The same month as the scene. It is why the record's presence is 'uncertain' rather than 'present', and writing it down is what makes that grade legible instead of unexplained.

roles.note: THE BOUND IS THE SOURCE'S, NOT THE MAN'S. This role is carried by the card's 1835 occupation block and is dated by what the cited source or sources are ABOUT, which is why `precision` can be no better than the span they cover. The span reaches 1835, so this role stands in the scene-date view. The printing the trade was read off is not on the card and is fetched by T-1254.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE LETTER LISTS (T-0378, T-0379). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here argues for a household, and this one argues for a PERSON. `data/residents/` cannot carry a person outside a household, so one was written around them and told to claim nothing — one member, no dwelling, no division, no trade, no family, no arrival beyond the paper's bound. tools/mint_letter_list_residents.py derives the set and prints every refusal, `--gate` proves no record here gained a roof, a trade or a second member, and docs/LIBERTIES.md L214 carries the change of scale.
